# Help-format corpus

[Compatibility matrix and live checks](../../../docs/compatibility.md) ·
[Development and validation](../../../docs/development.md#extended-tests-and-live-compatibility-reports)

`matrix.json` is the maintained list of 160 command paths, tiers, package names,
fixture filenames, expected flags and arguments, excluded forms, live sentinels,
and fixed version requests. Expected values are test assertions; they must not
be regenerated from parser output when a test fails.

The individual `.txt` files are compact, hand-authored format specimens with
paraphrased descriptions. They test argument shapes independently of installed
programs. The original FFmpeg, GCC, npm, and pip specimens were checked against
Ubuntu 24.04 output. The original VLC specimen is synthetic; a separate captured
VLC excerpt now provides real-format coverage.

The ten command-path specimens added on 2026-10-23 use the same selected local
help excerpts as `captured.json`. Their literal expectations are maintained
independently. `review-new-paths.json` adds two combined editing scenarios per
new path, including Unicode, repeated values, global options, positional
arguments, and child-command suffixes. Fixed help routes and rejection at runner
boundaries are checked in `test_review_fixes.py`.

`captured.json` contains bounded excerpts from installed programs on Ubuntu 24.04
under WSL. Each entry records its fixed source invocation, observed version,
and normalization. ANSI escapes and manual overstrikes are removed; selected
declaration lines and up to two continuation lines are placed under an explicit
Options heading. Local home/environment paths are replaced by placeholders.
Root npm retains its complete short help response. These are
excerpts, not complete manuals or snapshots of every option. The independently
maintained live sentinels and argument counts are also asserted against them.

The corpus includes nested command paths, alias spacing, `--[no-]` negation,
kubectl default values, AWS type labels, jq's two-value declarations, optional
Cargo values, and yt-dlp's partially optional templates. Tests also verify every
synthetic fixture flag's exact midline edit, required-value handling, global
options, positional boundaries, and fixed executable/manual probe arguments.

Concrete FFmpeg colon selectors are supported; incomplete/placeholder selectors
remain excluded. GCC comma-joined switches and generic 7-Zip brace declarations
are outside generic inference. They must not be
truncated into different flags. Root npm intentionally lacks option declarations;
usage examples must not become insertable flags. `npm-install.txt` separately
covers bracketed option groups, aliases, and repeated values.

`example-tool.1` is an original minimal roff page used for plain and gzip
manual-rendering tests. Compressed fixtures retain their original bytes.

`review-workflows.json` contains 47 explicit command-editing scenarios. Each
entry records a command path, pending line, selected flag, and expected line;
`@CURSOR@` denotes the character cursor before and after insertion. Expected
edits are literal fixtures, not values generated by the insertion implementation.

`review-additions.json` contains bounded local manual/help excerpts for Git
rebase, Docker build, and GNU find, recorded on 2026-10-23. Selected declaration
lines and two following lines are placed under an explicit OPTIONS heading;
these are incomplete excerpts. Versions and source labels accompany each entry.
Find's lowercase manual placeholders currently lack inferred argument metadata,
so its assertions establish flags and edits rather than required-value counts.
The [functional review](../../../docs/functional-review-2026-10-23.md) records
the live evidence and remaining limitations.

To extend coverage, add a matrix entry, a representative specimen, independently
chosen assertions, and a source-labelled captured excerpt when available. Add or
extend the relevant JSON driver when a special help route or subcommand path is
required. Keep unavailable live validation explicit. The harness installs no
packages; local downloads and environments belong in ignored `.cache/` storage,
and live reports belong in ignored `tests/reports/` storage.

## Workflow and Unix baseline corpus

`workflow-baseline.json` adds independent flags, exact argument placeholders,
optional-value expectations, exclusions, and live sentinels for 31 routes.
`workflow-baseline-captured.json` records observed installed versions, fixed
source requests, official references, and normalization for the associated
`workflow-*.txt` files. These are captured help, not generated option specimens;
Git manuals retain selected declaration lines and two following lines.
`workflow-manual-edge-cases.json` retains quoted Git examples and XZ numeric
preset-table rows from installed manuals. Those rows must not override real
option declarations or become partial insertable flags.

The corpus covers Git status/show/fetch/switch, six additional Compose leaves,
four Kubernetes leaves, GitHub issue/run/workflow list/view, and eleven Unix
utilities. GNU evidence does not establish BSD or BusyBox behavior. The XZ
numeric preset range is deliberately excluded. All expected flags and arity
remain independently specified; parser output must not regenerate expectations.

`test_workflow_baseline.py` checks route requests, schemas, required and optional
values, inherited arity, privacy, activation, and literal edits. The rendered
`test_workflow_terminal.py` checks actual Bash interaction, service/child
boundaries, repeated filters, sed expressions, cursor position, resize, and
scrollback. Its instrumented kubectl fixture records fixed help operands and
warm-cache behavior; it is separate from live installed-kubectl validation.

## Complete compatibility expansion

`expansion-systems.json` and `expansion-development.json` maintain independent
route-specific syntax expectations. Their entries are included in `matrix.json`
with an `expansion` marker. The original 59-case capture corpus retains its own
regressions; the two expansion test modules validate all new routes, profiles,
fixed requests, argument boundaries, and exact edits separately.

`expansion-systems-captured.json`, `expansion-development-captured.json`, and
their referenced capture files distinguish installed captures from hand-authored
documentation specimens. Provenance includes source URLs, request operands,
versions where observed, and normalization. Fixture-derived support is not live
execution evidence. `python-module-captured.json` contains six actual module help
captures, interpreter/module versions, and upstream links; both interpreter names
are covered by independent arity and Unicode insertion regressions.

Yarn Classic and modern captures retain distinct option surfaces. Missing tools
remain documented-fixture evidence until a live fixed help check is possible.
The FFmpeg curated selector profile follows the upstream
[stream-specifier reference](https://ffmpeg.org/ffmpeg.html#Stream-specifiers).

`followup-systems/` contains thirteen actual leaf-help captures from isolated
distribution packages and Python environments, with versions, fixed requests,
and upstream URLs in its manifest. These supplement the earlier format specimens.
`runtime-followup-captured.json` records eleven Go, .NET, Bun, and Arduino routes,
supplemental Go documentation, verified archive hashes, and exact installed-version
source excerpts for inherited options and hidden .NET aliases. Regressions keep
literal flag presence separate from independently reviewed arity contracts.
`followup-cloud-captured.json` supplies the six Azure/Google leaf routes and
supplemental global-option documentation, with actual versions and independent
arity expectations. Cloud credentials, login, initialization, and workload
requests are absent from this evidence.

## Explicit syntax captures

`syntax-7zip-captured.json` records fixed `-h` requests from installed `7z` and
`7zz` 23.01. `syntax-7z-x.txt` and `syntax-7zz-x.txt` retain selected switch
declarations. The static extraction profiles provide explicit attached-only
arity; generic parsing continues to exclude brace syntax. Matrix `profile_only`
and `documentation_path: []` separate static leaf edits from fixed root help.
The existing OpenSSH capture supplies selected bundle flags; independent tests
cover repetition, exact names, values, and the destination boundary. The
[syntax reference](../../../docs/argument-syntax.md) links upstream definitions
and documents exclusions. No archive extraction or SSH session is test evidence.
